data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Present continuous and present simple contrast

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Present continuous for actions happening now.
sections.explain: Present continuous uses am/is/are + verb + ing for actions happening now.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Present simple is used for habits and routines. 'He goes to work every day.'

answers.answer: He goes to work every day.
He is going to work every day.
He go to work every day.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: 'Now' signals present continuous: 'They are studying now.'

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Frequency words like 'always' are used with present simple.

answers.answer: She is always drinking coffee every day.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Temporary actions happening today use present continuous.

answers.answer: I am working at home today.
I am work at home today.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Negative present continuous: am/is/are + not + verb + ing.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Present simple negative uses don't/doesn't + base verb.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Questions invert be verb: 'Are they studying?'

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Contrast between routine and action happening now.
sections.explain: Use present simple for routine and present continuous for current action.

answers.answer: She works in an office, but today she is working at home.
She is working in an office every day.
She works at home now every day.
